Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

[{"id": "arka-english-main-0-prompt-long-0044", "row_sha256": "453db052a6646dcdf0805ff886f69e5857ec4c04fafd016ee59a25f27ed90ad4", "mode": "/prompt", "language": "en", "context": {}, "identity": false, "mode_instructions": "Organize the supplied request into a clear prompt. Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "hey, can you put together the request for a payroll export for Northline Workshop? this is for the May 1 through May 15, 2025 pay period, with a May 22 pay date. the point is to reconcile the payroll register against labor by department, not to make a new payroll calculation. use the payroll workbook named NW_Payroll_2025-05-15 as the source, and use entries received through May 16 at noon. i don't want the request to imply that anything has already been checked or approved.

The export should cover employees who were active for any part of that pay period. Leave out independent contractors, reimbursements, voided checks, and transactions dated outside the period. Include retroactive adjustments only when they are recorded in the source workbook as earnings for this period; don't pull in adjustments just because someone mentions them in a note. keep the file at the employee and earning-code level, with separate rows for separate cost centers, rather than rolling each person's pay into one total. We need to be able to trace each line back to its department.

Please make it a CSV, UTF-8, with commas as delimiters, one header row, and no merged cells or extra title rows. The columns should be in this order: employee ID, first name, last name, department code, department name, cost center, earning code, earning description, hours, rate, gross amount, pay period start, pay period end, and pay date. keep the employee ID as text so any leading zeros stay there. dates should use YYYY-MM-DD. I think two decimal places is enough for hours and money, but don't round a source amount just to force a total to match.

For earning codes, use the code and its description as stored in the workbook. Show regular hours and overtime hours as their own lines when those are separate earnings in the source; don't combine them into one hours figure. If an earnings row has no hours, leave hours blank rather than putting in zero, and if it has no rate, leave rate blank. For other required fields that are missing, keep the cell blank and list the affected employee ID and field in a separate exceptions note; please don't guess or fill it from another employee's record.

Order the rows by department code, then last name, first name, employee ID, earning code, and cost center. Use ascending order within each field. Preserve employee names as written in the workbook, including hyphens and accents. Don't change department codes or cost center values to make them look consistent. if a code is unclear, keep the source value and note it, rather than choosing what seems like the closest code.

Jasper is the only person who should receive the file: Jasper, not Amaya. The export includes compensation information, so don't copy Amaya, a department manager, or anyone else on the delivery message. The request should say to send the CSV through Northline's payroll secure folder and not as a regular email attachment. Don't include Social Security numbers, bank details, home addresses, dates of birth, or tax withholding elections, even if those happen to be visible elsewhere in the workbook.

Can the request also ask for a basic reconciliation check against the payroll register? compare the gross amount by department and the overall gross amount, using the source values, and flag any difference without changing the export to make the totals agree. If a comparison can't be made because a source value is missing, put that in the exceptions note. Don't state that the totals match unless that check has actually been performed. The note can identify the comparison and any differences, but it shouldn't repeat individual pay amounts.

Jasper said, “I only need the approved hours and earning codes for the period, and I need to be able to see which department each line belongs to.” That's why the department and cost center should stay on every applicable row, even where several lines have the same employee ID. The request should make clear that this is an export of the entries in the workbook, not a request to approve hours, correct payroll, or change anybody's pay.

Please ask for one file named Northline_May01-15_2025_Payroll.csv and the separate exceptions note, if there are exceptions. Don't ask for a spreadsheet version, a PDF, or a second export by department. The note should be stored in the same secure folder as the CSV, and should refer to employees by ID rather than full name. If there are no exceptions, the request doesn't need to require an empty note; it can simply say that no note is needed in that case.

The final paragraph should mention that the export is for the payroll reconciliation review for this pay period only. It should not describe a future process or imply a deadline that i haven't supplied. Keep the whole request usable as a brief someone can follow, with the recipient instruction prominent and the limits on the included data easy to find.", "output": "Please prepare a payroll export for Northline Workshop for the May 1–15, 2025 pay period (pay date: May 22). Use the payroll workbook **NW_Payroll_2025-05-15** as the source and include entries received through May 16 at noon. This export is for reconciling the payroll register against labor by department; it is not a new payroll calculation. Do not imply that any checks have already been performed or that the export has been approved.

Include employees who were active for any part of the pay period. Exclude independent contractors, reimbursements, voided checks, and transactions dated outside the period. Include retroactive adjustments only when the source workbook records them as earnings for this period; do not include adjustments merely mentioned in a note. Create separate rows for each employee and earning code, and separate rows for different cost centers. Do not roll an employee’s pay into a single total. Keep each line traceable to its department.

Create a UTF-8 CSV with comma delimiters, one header row, and no merged cells or extra title rows. Use these columns in this exact order:

1. Employee ID
2. First name
3. Last name
4. Department code
5. Department name
6. Cost center
7. Earning code
8. Earning description
9. Hours
10. Rate
11. Gross amount
12. Pay period start
13. Pay period end
14. Pay date

Keep employee IDs as text so leading zeros are preserved. Format dates as YYYY-MM-DD. Use two decimal places for hours and money, but do not round source amounts to force a total to match.

Use earning codes and descriptions as stored in the workbook. Keep regular and overtime hours on separate lines when they are separate earnings in the source; do not combine them into one hours figure. If an earnings row has no hours or rate, leave that cell blank rather than entering zero. Leave other missing required fields blank and list the affected employee ID and field in a separate exceptions note. Do not guess or copy information from another employee’s record.

Sort rows in ascending order by department code, last name, first name, employee ID, earning code, and cost center. Preserve names as written in the workbook, including hyphens and accents. Do not alter department codes or cost center values for consistency. If a code is unclear, retain the source value and note it rather than selecting a seemingly similar code.

Send the file to **Jasper, not Amaya**. Jasper is the only recipient. Because the export contains compensation information, do not copy Amaya, a department manager, or anyone else on the delivery message. Send the CSV through Northline’s payroll secure folder, not as a regular email attachment. Do not include Social Security numbers, bank details, home addresses, dates of birth, or tax withholding elections, even if they are visible elsewhere in the workbook.

Also perform a basic reconciliation check against the payroll register. Compare gross amount by department and overall gross amount using the source values. Flag any difference without changing the export to make totals agree. If a comparison cannot be made because a source value is missing, record that in the exceptions note. Do not state that totals match unless the check has actually been performed. The note may identify the comparison and any differences, but must not repeat individual pay amounts.

Jasper said, “I only need the approved hours and earning codes for the period, and I need to be able to see which department each line belongs to.” Keep the department and cost center on every applicable row, including when multiple lines share an employee ID. Make clear that this is an export of the workbook entries, not a request to approve hours, correct payroll, or change anyone’s pay.

Provide one file named **Northline_May01-15_2025_Payroll.csv** and a separate exceptions note if there are exceptions. Do not provide a spreadsheet version, PDF, or second export by department. Store the note in the same secure folder as the CSV, and identify employees in the note by ID rather than full name. If there are no exceptions, no note is needed.

This export is for the payroll reconciliation review for this pay period only. Do not describe a future process or imply a deadline."}]
